##### Analyzing fluid biomarkers for association with cognitive status.

##### Biomarker core and Data core collaboration.

```{r , echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library("gtsummary")
Biomarker_Data2 <- Biomarker_Data %>% filter(Cognitive_Status == "Cognitively unimpaired" | Cognitive_Status == "MCI" | Cognitive_Status == "AD") %>% filter(Race == "White" | Race == "Black") %>% dplyr::select(Cognitive_Status, tau, pT181, aBeta42, aBeta40, `aBeta 42:40`, pT217, GFAP, NfL, APOE_Coll, BMI, Age, Race, sex,  Education_Coll, Stroke,	Cancer,	Diabetes,	MI, `Depression in last 2yrs`,	Hypertension,	Hypercholesterolemia,	`Sleep Apnea`,	`Atrial Fibrillation`)
Biomarker_Data2 %>% tbl_summary(missing_text = "(Missing)", label = c(BMI ~ "BMI (pg/mL)", tau ~ "tTau (pg/mL)", pT181 ~ "pT181 (pg/mL)", aBeta42 ~ "aB42 (pg/mL)", aBeta40 ~ "aB40 (pg/mL)", `aBeta 42:40` ~ "aBeta 42:40", GFAP ~ "GFAP (pg/mL)",pT217 ~ "pT217 (pg/mL)", NfL ~ "NfL (pg/mL)", Education_Coll ~ "Education", APOE_Coll ~ "APOE" ), digits = list(everything() ~ c(3))) %>% bold_labels() %>% modify_caption("**Summary table**")
```

##### Now we will see the summary of all variables by diagnosis categories. 

```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
Biomarker_Data2 %>% filter(Cognitive_Status == "Cognitively unimpaired" | Cognitive_Status == "MCI" | Cognitive_Status == "AD") %>% filter(Race == "White" | Race == "Black") %>%
  tbl_summary(
    by = Cognitive_Status,
    statistic = list(all_continuous() ~ "{mean} ({sd}) | {median} ({IQR})",
                     all_categorical() ~ "{n} / {N} ({p}%)"),
    digits = list(everything() ~ c(3)),
    label = c(BMI ~ "BMI (pg/mL)", tau ~ "tTau (pg/mL)", pT181 ~ "pT181 (pg/mL)", aBeta42 ~ "aB42 (pg/mL)", aBeta40 ~ "aB40 (pg/mL)", GFAP ~ "GFAP (pg/mL)", NfL ~ "NfL (pg/mL)", pT217 ~ "pT217 (pg/mL)", Education_Coll ~ "Education", APOE_Coll ~ "APOE", `aBeta 42:40` ~ "aBeta 42:40" ),
    missing_text = "(Missing)"
  ) %>% add_p() %>% bold_labels() %>% modify_caption("**Summary table: Different cognitive status**")
```





#### Correlation Plot:


```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
datamat1 = cor(Data_corr[,c(2,3,4,5,6,11, 12, 13)], use="pairwise.complete.obs")

```

##### Q-Q Plots: 


```{r, include=FALSE}
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(qqplotr)
```




```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
Biomarker_Data21 = pivot_longer(Biomarker_Data2, cols = c(2,3,4,5,6, 7,8, 9, 11))
my_qqplott = function(.data, .title) {
  ggplot(data= .data, mapping = aes(sample = value)) + stat_qq_band(alpha = 0.05) + stat_qq_line()  + stat_qq_point() + facet_wrap(~ name, scales = "free") + 
    labs(x = "Theoretical Quantiles", y = "Sample Quantiles", title = .title)
}
```


```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
qqplots = Biomarker_Data21 %>% split(.$name) %>% imap(my_qqplott)
```


```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
qqplots$aBeta40
qqplots$aBeta42
qqplots$`aBeta 42:40`
qqplots$pT181
qqplots$tau
qqplots$GFAP
qqplots$NfL
qqplots$BMI

```



#### Standarized the Biomarkers: $(X_{ij} - \mu_{j}) / \sigma_{j}$, where $X_{ij}$ is the $i_{th}$ observation for the $j_{th}$ variable, $\mu_{j}$ is the mean of the variable $X_{j}$, and $\sigma_{j}$ is the variance of the variable $X_{j}$. 




```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

Biomarker_Dataa <- Biomarker_Data %>% dplyr::select(Cognitive_Status, tau, pT181, aBeta42, aBeta40,pT217, GFAP, NfL, APOE_Coll, BMI, Age, Race, sex,  Education_Coll,  Stroke,	Cancer,	Diabetes,	MI, `Depression in last 2yrs`,	Hypertension,	Hypercholesterolemia,	`Sleep Apnea`,`Atrial Fibrillation`) 
Biomarker_Dataa[2 : 8] <- as.data.frame(scale(Biomarker_Dataa[2 : 8]))
Biomarker_Dataa[10] <- as.data.frame(scale(Biomarker_Dataa[10]))
Biomarker_Dataa$ratio_of_aB42_and_40 = Biomarker_Dataa$aBeta42/Biomarker_Dataa$aBeta40
Biomarker_Dataa$ratio_of_p181_and_aB42 = Biomarker_Dataa$pT181/Biomarker_Dataa$aBeta42
Biomarker_Dataa$Education_Coll = as.factor(Biomarker_Dataa$Education_Coll)

```


##### Forest Plot

```{r, echo=FALSE, include=FALSE}
library(ggplot2)
library(metafor)
library(ggpubr)
library(dplyr)
```



```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
Forest_plot_data = Biomarker_Dataa %>% dplyr::select( pT181, pT217, APOE_Coll, BMI, Age, Race, sex,  Education_Coll, GFAP, NfL,tau, aBeta42, aBeta40, ratio_of_aB42_and_40, ratio_of_p181_and_aB42, Stroke,	Cancer,	Diabetes,	MI, `Depression in last 2yrs`,	Hypertension,	Hypercholesterolemia,	`Sleep Apnea`,`Atrial Fibrillation`)
Forest_plot_data[1 : 2] <- as.data.frame(scale(Forest_plot_data[1 : 2]))
#model
model_pT181 = lm(pT181 ~ APOE_Coll + BMI + Age + Race + sex +  Education_Coll + GFAP+ NfL + tau + aBeta42 + aBeta40 + ratio_of_aB42_and_40 + ratio_of_p181_and_aB42 + Stroke +	Cancer +	Diabetes +	MI + `Depression in last 2yrs`+	Hypertension +	Hypercholesterolemia +	`Sleep Apnea` +	`Atrial Fibrillation`, data = Forest_plot_data)
model_pT217 = lm(pT217 ~ APOE_Coll + BMI + Age + Race + sex +  Education_Coll + GFAP+ NfL + tau + aBeta42 + aBeta40 + ratio_of_aB42_and_40 + ratio_of_p181_and_aB42 + Stroke +	Cancer +	Diabetes +	MI + `Depression in last 2yrs`+	Hypertension +	Hypercholesterolemia +	`Sleep Apnea` +	`Atrial Fibrillation`, data = Forest_plot_data)

#Extract coefficients

coef_pT181 = coef(summary(model_pT181))
coef_pT217 = coef(summary(model_pT217))
#coef_pT181 = coef_pT181[- "(Intercept)"]
coef_pT181 = coef_pT181[- 1,]
coef_pT217 = coef_pT217[- 1,]

forest_data1 = data.frame(
  Variable = rownames(coef_pT181),
  coef_pTau181 = coef_pT181[,"Estimate"],
  SE_pTau181 = coef_pT181[,"Std. Error"],
  P_pTau181 = coef_pT181[,"Pr(>|t|)"]
)

forest_data2 = data.frame(
  Variable = rownames(coef_pT217),
  coef_pTau217 = coef_pT217[,"Estimate"],
  SE_pTau217 = coef_pT217[,"Std. Error"],
  P_pTau217 = coef_pT217[,"Pr(>|t|)"]
)
#Create Forest plot

forest_plot1 = ggplot(forest_data1, aes(y = Variable)) + 
  geom_point(aes(x = coef_pTau181, color = "pT181"), size = 1) + geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = coef_pTau181 - 1.96*SE_pTau181, xmax = coef_pTau181 + 1.96*SE_pTau181, color = "pT181"), height = 0.15)  + scale_color_manual(values = c("pT181" = "blue")) + labs(x = "coefficient", y = "Variable", title = "Forest Plot of Association", subtitle = "Z score of pT181", caption = "(Mean) 95% Confidence Intervals") +  theme_minimal()
#+ geom_point(aes(x = coef_pTau217, color = "pT217"), size = 1) + geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = coef_pTau217 - 1.96*SE_pTau217, xmax = coef_pTau217 + 1.96*SE_pTau217, color = "pT217"), height = 0.15)
# #, "pT217" = "red"
forest_plot2 = ggplot(forest_data2, aes(y = Variable)) + 
  geom_point(aes(x = coef_pTau217, color = "pT217"), size = 1) + geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = coef_pTau217 - 1.96*SE_pTau217, xmax = coef_pTau217 + 1.96*SE_pTau217, color = "pT217"), height = 0.15)  + scale_color_manual(values = c("pT217" = "red")) + labs(x = "coefficient", y = "Variable", title = "Forest Plot of Association", subtitle = "Z score of pT217", caption = "(Mean) 95% Confidence Intervals") +  theme_minimal()
#forest_plot1 = ggplot(forest_data1, aes(y = Variable)) + 
 # geom_point(aes(x = coef_pTau181, color = "pT181"), size = 1) + geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = coef_pTau181 - 1.96*SE_pTau181, xmax = coef_pTau181 + 1.96*SE_pTau181, color = "pT181"), height = 0.15) + geom_point(aes(x = coef_pTau217, color = "pT217"), size = 1) + geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = coef_pTau217 - 1.96*SE_pTau217, xmax = coef_pTau217 + 1.96*SE_pTau217, color = "pT217"), height = 0.15) + scale_color_manual(values = c("pT181" = "blue", "pT217" = "red")) + labs(x = "coefficient", y = "Variable", title = "Forest Plot of Association", subtitle = "Z score of pT181 and pT217", caption = "(Mean) 95% Confidence Intervals") +  theme_minimal()

Figure = ggarrange(forest_plot1, forest_plot2, labels = c("A", "B"), ncol = 2, nrow = 1)
Figure
```

#### Splitting the data using Cross Validation method: 


```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
#Splitting train and test data
Biomarker_Data11 = Biomarker_Dataa
Biomarker_Dataa = Biomarker_Data11 %>% filter(Cognitive_Status == "Cognitively unimpaired" | Cognitive_Status == "MCI" | Cognitive_Status == "AD") %>% filter(Race == "White" | Race == "Black")
Biomarker_Dataa = na.omit(Biomarker_Dataa)

#Biomarker_Data2
#library(openxlsx)
#write.xlsx(Biomarker_Dataa, file = "Biomarker_Final_Data.xlsx")
```









```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
set.seed(154)
#test.size = 0.3
#test_index = createDataPartition(Biomarker_Dataa$Cognitive_Status, p = test.size, list = FALSE)
#train1 = Biomarker_Dataa[-test_index, ]
#test1 = Biomarker_Dataa[test_index,]
nrFolds = 5
folds = rep_len(1:nrFolds, nrow(Biomarker_Dataa))
folds = sample(folds, nrow(Biomarker_Dataa))
for(k in 1:nrFolds) {
  fold = which(folds == k)
  train1 = Biomarker_Dataa[-fold,]
  test1 = Biomarker_Dataa[fold,]
}
```

```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=FALSE}
p2 = predict(mod_dem, test1, type = 'class')
confusionMatrix(p2, test1$Cognitive_Status)

rs4 = r[['rocs']]

Ad_MCI = rs4[[3]][[2]]

plot.roc(Ad_MCI, add = T, col = 'red')
plot.roc(CU_MCI, add = T, col = 'green')
legend("topright", c("CU_AD", "Ad_MCI", "CU_MCI"), lty=1,col = c("blue", "red", "green"), bty = "n")


CognitivelyUnimpaired_AD = auc(CU_AD)
AD_MCI = auc(Ad_MCI)
CognitivelyUnimpaired_MCI = auc(CU_MCI)
AUC = rbind(CognitivelyUnimpaired_AD, CognitivelyUnimpaired_MCI,AD_MCI )
colnames(AUC) = c("AUC")
AUC
```

```{r, warning=FALSE, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, include=FALSE}
mod_dem4_OR = tbl_regression(mod_dem4, exponentiate = TRUE , label = list( Education_Coll ~ "Education")) %>% bold_labels() %>% modify_caption("**Demographic + pT181 + pT217 Model**")
mod_dem4_OR
###### Interpretation: 

###### White participants are 64% less likely than the Black participants to fall in the MCI group than the normal cognition. 

###### Male participants are 114% more likely than the female participants to fall in the MCI group than normal cognition. 

###### Higher pT217 in the MCI group than normal cognition group. 

###### Lower pT181 in the MCI group than normal cognition group.

###### Male participants are 333% more likely than the female participants to fall in the AD group than normal cognition. 

###### Higher educated people are 76% less likely than the lower educated people to fall in the AD group than the normal cognition. 

###### Higher pT217 in the AD group than normal cognition group. 

###### Lower pT181 in the AD group than normal cognition group.
```

##### Stepwise Regression with backward Selection: 

```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
require(nnet)
library(tidyverse)
library(caret)
library(MASS)
train1= na.omit(train1)
#intercept_only <- multinom(Cognitive_Status ~ 1, data=train1)
mod1 = multinom(Cognitive_Status ~ pT217  + tau + pT181 + GFAP +  NfL + APOE_Coll + Education_Coll + Age + BMI + sex + Race, data = train1)
#, method = "cv", number = 10 ratio_of_p181_and_aB42  + ratio_of_aB42_and_40 +
#summary(mod1)
#
#vif(mod1)
library(car)
```



```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
mod_step = step(mod1, direction = 'backward', trace=0)
```


```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
summary(mod_step)
```

##### Odds Ratio and 95 \% CI

```{r, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE,  message=FALSE}
Step_model = tbl_regression(mod_step, exponentiate = TRUE) %>% bold_labels() %>% modify_caption("**Stepwise Model: Backward selection**")
Step_model

```


###### Interpretation: 

###### White participants are 66% less likely than the Black participants to fall in the MCI group than the normal cognition. 

###### Male participants are 151% more likely than the female participants to fall in the MCI group than normal cognition. 

###### Higher(120%) pT217 in the MCI group than normal cognition group. 


###### Male participants are 497% more likely than the female participants to fall in the AD group than normal cognition. 

###### Higher educated people are 71% less likely than the lower educated people to fall in the AD group than the normal cognition. 

###### Participants with 'no e4' are 65% less likely than participants with any e4 to fall in the AD group than normal cognition. 

###### Higher pT217 in the AD group than normal cognition group. 

###### Higher GFAP in the AD group than normal cognition group.
